title: k8s-node-provisioning-incident-notes
body:
SUMMARY:
Working notes and breadcrumbs for the node provisioning flakiness observed in cluster-prod-west-2 during the 2026-02-24 deploy window. Intermittent failures where new nodes join but kubelet either fails to register or becomes NotReady after pulling images. Repro rate ~2/10 nodes.

WHAT I SAW (raw commands + outputs):
1) kubectl get nodes -o wide
   node-az1-12   NotReady   3m   v1.26.4   10.0.12.34   <none>    <none>   

2) kubectl describe node node-az1-12 (excerpt)
   Conditions:
     Ready    False   KubeletNotReady   kubelet stopped posting status
   Events:
     2m   Warning   NodeNotReady   Node node-az1-12 status is now: NodeNotReady

3) ssh to host -> sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 60
   (important lines)
   Feb 24 22:11:03 kubelet[2345]: E0224 22:11:03.123456   2345 kubelet.go:2352] Node did not register: timed out waiting for the condition
   Feb 24 22:11:03 kubelet[2345]: E0224 22:11:03.123789   2345 server.go:123] failed to run kubelet: error creating kubelet: failed to start cAdvisor: error getting rootfs info: stat /rootfs: no such file or directory

4) journalctl -u cloud-init -b | grep -i error
   22:10:49 cloud-init[1345]: Error fetching metadata: HTTP 404 from metadata server
   22:10:55 cloud-init[1357]: write /var/lib/cloud/instances/..data: no space left on device (we saw this on one repro)

5) docker/containerd outputs on some hosts:
   containerd: failed to start containerd-shim: exit status 1
   image pull backoff: unauthorized: authentication required

6) helm upgrade --install core-agent ./charts/core-agent -n kube-system --values values-prod.yaml
   -> on a NotReady node the daemonset pod fails with CrashLoopBackOff; kubectl logs show mount errors:
   MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "var-lib-data" : hostPath type check failed: expected Directory or Create, got File

HYPOTHESES (ordered by likelihood):
- H1: cloud-init race -> root filesystem layout different (rootfs not mounted at expected /rootfs) causing kubelet startup failure. Evidence: kubelet complaining about /rootfs and cloud-init errors on metadata and disk writes.
- H2: AMI drift: image used by autoscaler has a different partitioning or has stale leftover files causing hostPath mounts to fail (hostPath type check failed).
- H3: ephemeral disk full on some instance types in AZ1 due to leftover logs/artifacts -> causes cloud-init writes to fail and kubelet can't start correctly.
- H4: container registry auth intermittent -> causes daemonset failures but not primary reason for node NotReady (secondary).

WHAT I TRIED (commands + notes):
- Repro locally by spinning up a node using the same ASG launch template in staging. Observed cloud-init 404 to metadata in one case.
- SSHed into instance and checked mount layout: ls -la /rootfs -> returned: "No such file or directory" on affected host. On healthy host /rootfs exists and has /proc,/sys bind mounts.
- manully re-created /rootfs as directory and rebind mounted expected dirs as a test:
    sudo mkdir -p /rootfs
    sudo mount --bind /proc /rootfs/proc
    sudo mount --bind /sys /rootfs/sys
  After this, kubelet restarted and briefly became Ready (test only).
- Checked AMI build output for last bake: packer logs show cloud-init v22.3 but the bake used a different cloud-init config than prod (missing mount tasks). Filing note in PR-1284.
- For hostPath mount failure: inspected the path on host: /var/lib/core-agent/data existed as a file on some images (packaging bug).
- Verified disk usage: df -h -> on one repro node /dev/nvme0n1p1 100% used. correlate with cloud-init no space error.

OPEN ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS:
- A1: Add extra validation to the AMI bake step: confirm /rootfs present and is a directory, ensure expected bind-mount tasks are in cloud-init user-data. (Assigned to Jordan) (JIRA-CS-3421).
- A2: Add a pre-boot check in the ASG lifecycle (systemd unit) to fail early and log clear message if /rootfs missing or disk < 10% free. (Assigned to me)
- A3: Patch helm chart for core-agent to avoid strict hostPath type check until AMI fixed (workaround). Add toleration and initContainer to create directory as required. (PR draft referenced: github PR-1284).
- A4: Add CloudWatch metric/alert for cloud-init failure counts in ASG for quicker detection. (Emily to own)

NOTES TO SELF / FRAGMENTS:
- When node registers but Immediately NotReady: check kubelet handshake -> possible TLS bootstrap failure if kubelet token not rotated. But not likely here (logs show rootfs).
- Watch for pattern by AZ (seems concentrated in az1). Could be a bad AMI rollout to that AZ only.
- If we fix AMI, run 50-node canary replacement via rolling update of ASG.

REFERENCES:
- Ticket: JIRA-CS-3421 (incident doc and timeline)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/PR-1284 (AMI bake config + cloud-init changes)
- Slack: #infra-node-provisioning thread-abc123 (live debugging)

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add AMI validation script to packer pipeline (low effort)
- [ ] Add initContainer to core-agent helm chart to create hostPath dir (short-term)
- [ ] Schedule canary ASG with updated AMI and monitor for 24h

END OF NOTES.

If I forget: follow up with Jordan for AMI bake logs and ticket owner on CS-3421. Keep this file as scratchpad until we close incident.
